response.sql: WITH large AS (SELECT o.account_id, d.A3 AS region, o.amount FROM `order` o JOIN account a ON a.account_id = o.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id WHERE o.amount >= 2802), grp AS (SELECT account_id, region, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount FROM large GROUP BY account_id, region), overall AS (SELECT AVG(avg_amount) AS overall_avg FROM grp) SELECT g.account_id, g.region, g.avg_amount, g.avg_amount - o.overall_avg AS difference FROM grp g CROSS JOIN overall o ORDER BY difference DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The cutoff is inclusive, so orders with amount >= 2802 count as large. The request does not say whether 2802 itself is included.
Every row in the order table is a standing order; no k_symbol or date filter is applied, since the request does not name one.
Inner joins drop orders whose account_id has no account row, and accounts whose district_id has no district row. Each account has a single district, so each account maps to one region.
The SQL targets SQLite (the schema uses backtick-quoted `order` and SQLite-style types). The overall figure is the unweighted mean of the per-(account, region) averages, and the output is unrounded.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is exclusive: only orders with amount strictly greater than 2802 count as large.
